events.summary:
...Forecast flooding changed to Minor severity and increased in
duration for the following rivers in New Mexico...

Rio Chama Below Chamita affecting Rio Arriba County.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Rio Chama below Chamita.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 6.0 feet, Properties in the flood plain along the Rio
Chama and near the junction of the Rio Ojo Caliente will see water
in their yards. Impacts can include bank erosion and damage to
wells and septic tanks.  These impacts will increase in severity at
higher river levels.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 11:00 AM MDT Tuesday the stage was 6.6 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 5.5 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 11:00 AM MDT Tuesday was 6.7 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 6.9 feet
this afternoon.
- Flood stage is 6.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 6.9
feet on 06/13/1991.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/abq/EmergencyPrepFlood

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in New
Mexico...

Rio Puerco Near Bernardo affecting Socorro County.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is occurring and minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Rio Puerco near Bernardo.

* WHEN...Until Thursday evening.

* IMPACTS...At the initial flood stage of 19.5 feet, the water level
in the Lower Rio Puerco will begin to threaten several homes and
structures in the village of San Francisco between Interstate 25
and the Rio Grande. Further rises in water levels would begin to
flood the village of San Francisco.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 11:00 AM MDT Tuesday the stage was 20.4 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 18.0 feet.
- Recent Activity...The maximum river stage in the 24 hours ending
at 11:00 AM MDT Tuesday was 24.3 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 21.4 feet
tomorrow morning. It will then fall below flood stage Thursday
morning.
- Flood stage is 19.5 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 19.5
feet on 08/10/2006 and a similar crest on 10/03 of this current
month.
- http://www.weather.gov/abq/EmergencyPrepFlood
